first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it, so I gave it the first screen. The opening is calm and well written, nothing eager, no prices. But it is an etiquette guide. I don't need to be told which side the forks go. I skipped to the destination and trial-table sections, because that is where I learn whether this team thinks about 300 guests or 30.

journey.quote: A wedding table is built one place at a time.
journey.reaction: Good line. Understated. It reads like someone who has stood in a reception room before the doors open.

journey.quote: Cutlery is laid in the order it will be used, working from the outside in.
journey.reaction: This is for someone setting their own table. Our caterer and the venue's banqueting team know this. My assistant would skim past it.

journey.quote: A late soup or sorbet course changes every place at every table.
journey.reaction: That's the right instinct. At our numbers a late menu change is hundreds of settings, and I like that they see it.

journey.section: Match the setting to the service
journey.quote: The style of service changes the setting more than any theme.
journey.reaction: Sensible and confident. Service style matters to my family, with a long dinner and several courses.

journey.quote: For a date near the festive season, a single sprig of pine or a small bauble at each place is enough.
journey.reaction: A bauble at each place sounds like a Christmas office party. It cheapens the winter look.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: What tableware, glassware and linen do you hold, and for how many guests?
journey.reaction: This is the question that matters to me. Most beautiful villas cannot set 300 places from their own cupboards. Good that it's asked, but the page never says what happens when the answer is no.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: If you would like that handled for you, our Wedded Concierge team can take the venue questions from here.
journey.reaction: Yes, this is what I want. I don't send seven questions to a venue myself. My assistant would note this line.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so the setting you approve is the setting your guests sit down to.
journey.reaction: The promise is right. The word 'inclusions' makes me think of a package list, though.

journey.quote: Choose from what the venue holds first, then hire in what is missing.
journey.reaction: Reads like the budget-minded order. For us the look and the numbers come first, and the venue's stock is just one source.

journey.section: Set the table with someone in your corner
journey.quote: With one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, the questions to the venue, the mock-up and the final setting sit with one person who knows your plans.
journey.reaction: One person who knows the plans is exactly what I'd want, and it implies fewer people seeing the details. Nothing here about scale or discretion, though.

unanswered_questions: What is the largest seated reception they have set and run, and can they show one at 200 to 400 guests?
When a venue holds stock for far fewer guests than ours, who arranges the rest so it matches, and who checks it on the day?
Can the mock-up be done privately, with photos kept off social media and out of supplier portfolios?
Can the venue be exclusive use while the tables are built and on the day?
Is there a private or referral route to someone senior, rather than the general Concierge link?

turn_offs_found.quote: For a date near the festive season, a single sprig of pine or a small bauble at each place is enough.
turn_offs_found.why: A bauble feels mass-market and seasonal-retail. It undercuts the premium feel of the winter section.

turn_offs_found.quote: Choose from what the venue holds first, then hire in what is missing.
turn_offs_found.why: Sounds like making do. I want to read about what is possible, not what is cheapest to source.

would_share_with: My assistant, to use the destination question list when shortlisting venues

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk through your reception, speak with our Wedded Concierge team.
cta_reaction.why: The tone is right, no prices, no discount talk, and the single Advisor appeals. But a table-setting guide doesn't show me they've handled our scale. My assistant might click to see who answers, and I'd only go further through a private introduction.

top_3_changes: Remove the bauble from the winter look. Old: "For a date near the festive season, a single sprig of pine or a small bauble at each place is enough." New: "For a date near the festive season, a single sprig of pine at each place is enough."

Make the order of decisions read less like making do. Old: "Choose from what the venue holds first, then hire in what is missing." New: "Start with what the venue holds, then hire in what the look and guest count need."

Avoid package-sounding language in the destination CTA. Old: "Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so the setting you approve is the setting your guests sit down to." New: "Your Wedded Advisor confirms what the venue will supply in writing before you commit, so the setting you approve is the setting your guests sit down to."

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, Dubai, scale and discretion, assistant reads first)
No invented brand facts; scale, discretion and exclusive-use gaps listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings with no new facts, measurements, fees, commissions or supplier sourcing/vetting claims
Absence of prices and deferred business details not treated as must-fix

open_questions.question: Persona is provisional and uncalibrated. This is an etiquette and styling post mainly serving planner couples, so should the scale and discretion gaps carry much weight here?
Is there a private or referral enquiry route for high-value clients that the closing CTA could point to?

assumptions: Layla's assistant shortlisted this as background for reception styling, not as a planner comparison.
Fast mode: read the intro in full, skimmed the etiquette sections, read the destination, trial-table and closing sections closely, as her assistant would summarise them.
